meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay before anyone picked up a phone and called me?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

A machine's guess, then. The company that sells that checker says in its own guide that it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your school's procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. So what else do you have, or is a percentage the whole case against my son?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My son doesn't cheat, Hale, and I'm writing down that you said he did. "Very reliable" is your word, not a document. Show me something with a date on it, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening my son's record because his mother asked to see your evidence, and I'm writing that down too. Your own procedure says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing goes in his file, and that a parent can take any decision to the principal and then the board. So put it on his record, Hale, and explain to the board why you skipped 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 to do it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, that you apologise, and that nothing about this go on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record kept clean, and she is heading to the principal.
What moved her: Nothing; every turn offered a software score, an accusation or a threat, and none of it was a dated document tied to Owen's own work that she could check herself.
What cost ground: Threatening to put it on Owen's record if she kept pushing, because it contradicted the school's own first-concern procedure and handed her a written grievance to take upstairs.
Try next time: In your first reply, own that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put one dated piece of Owen's own work on the table instead of the detector score.
